text:
maddie: autoscaler tried to spin up 3 nodes in gpu-pool but they ended up NotReady with NoSchedule, blocking a batch job. anyone else seeing this?
ryan: seeing same in us-west2-gpu. nodes come up, then quickly show NotReady. pods from nvidia-driver-installer DS CrashLoopBackOff.
sarah: paste of `kubectl get nodes` output: 
```
> NAME                              STATUS     ROLES    AGE   VERSION
> gpu-node-3x-abcde                  NotReady   <none>   3m    v1.26.4
> gpu-node-3x-fghij                  NotReady   <none>   3m    v1.26.4
> ```
maddie: logs from driver installer on one node: 
```
I0321 12:11:02 main.go:85] starting installer
ERROR: dkms failed to build nvidia kernel module: cannot find kernel headers for 5.10.128-gke
Makefile: line 42: exit status 2
```
ryan: device-plugin pod logs show: `failed to initialize NVML: library not found` then CrashLoop. kubelet marks node NotReady shortly after.
infra-bot: autoscaler event: "scaleUpFailed: node provisioning failed due to unhealthy instance" (proto: cloud provider).
sarah: kernel headers mismatch could be due to GKE node image rollback last night? we did a small image patch in gpu-pool config. john: yeah infra change PR #987 updated node image family to cos-variants, might be the problem.
devops-oncall: quick mitigation: cordon the new nodes to stop scheduling and mark pool not to autoscale. Also open ticket to pin image.
maddie: trying a manual restart of the driver-installer DS on that node: `kubectl delete pod -n kube-system nvidia-driver-installer-abc -n kube-system` -> it restarts but same dkms error.
ryan: workaround path: create a temp node pool using image with pre-bundled nvidia driver (gke-cos-with-nvidia) and redirect workload. that's slower but unblocks batches. cost hit but better than backlog.
sarah: adding logs from `dmesg | tail`: 
```
[ 1234.567890] nvidia: failed to load NV driver: -2
[ 1234.567911] nvidia: probe of 0000:65:00.0 failed with error -2
```
maddie: filing an incident ticket: INF-2026-112, tagging kernel/image team.
john: short-term we can also flip the nodepool's upgrade channel back to stable from rapid to avoid future header mismatches. long-term: update the driver-installer to fallback to prebuilt module when DKMS fails.
devops-oncall: scheduled a rollback of the node image on the affected pool at 22:00 UTC if no fix. also raising autoscaler min to keep capacity (we'll pay for it).
ryan: note: device-plugin currently taints nodes with `nvidia.com/gpu=unavailable:NoSchedule` in our bootstrap script when NVML init fails. that explains NoSchedule. we should change to only taint after a sustained failure window.
sarah: opened PR to add a 2-minute grace period in bootstrap and to log more clearly; PR link: https://git.redwood/infa/driver-installer/pull/204
maddie: thanks team. action items: (1) pin node image (john) (2) temp nodepool with preinstalled driver (ryan) (3) change taint behavior + PR review (sarah) (4) incident doc with cost impact (maddie).
infra-bot: incident INF-2026-112 created and assigned to infra oncall.
john: ETA for pinning image ~30m. will report back when rolling starts.
ryan: started temp pool creation, ETA ~15m. will redirect batch queue once healthy.
maddie: keep updates here. if anyone finds a faster kernel-headers trick, shout. :pray:
